clue.text: Second element to go wrong

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, so this word gives back
fire is one of the four classical elements

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson where the next element tried goes badly.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plan backfires it fails, rebounding on its maker.

clue.text: Bare victory for Stanley

parts.note: bald means bare, without covering
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A narrow, unadorned triumph scored by someone called Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a British Conservative Prime Minister between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin was three times Prime Minister of Britain, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Are you, say, involved with 17? How idiotic!

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: spoken, the words are you sound like the letters R and U
the solution to 17-down, a part of something

explanation.surface: A rude question about someone's part, followed by an exclamation at their stupidity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes R, U and the seven letters of 17-down into one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretinous is an old insulting word for very stupid, a synonym of idiotic.

clue.text: Mugger's corn-plaster?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a street robber keeps a corn-plaster about him.
explanation.walkthrough: A footpad was a highway robber on foot, an old word for a mugger; read as two words it is a pad for the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An old robber who worked on foot rather than horseback, and a cushioning dressing worn under the sole or toe.

clue.text: Engineers, forsooth, join up again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
marry is an archaic oath meaning indeed, like forsooth

explanation.surface: Army sappers, speaking old-fashioned English, sign on once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed a second time is to be joined in matrimony anew.

clue.text: Dan Cupid

explanation.surface: Two names stood side by side, as if one man were called Dan Cupid.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Archer was the patriarch of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap about country folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The farmer in a long-running British radio serial bore this surname, and the god of love shoots arrows with a bow.

clue.text: Stuff that's mostly lost on Kubla

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: astray means lost, off the right path
Kubla Khan, the Mongol ruler of Coleridge's poem

explanation.surface: Something largely wasted on the Mongol emperor of Coleridge's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from ASTRAY, leaving ASTRA; 'on' just joins it to KHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a curly fleece fabric, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: The failure of a barber

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a hairdresser who flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: To come a cropper is a British idiom for a heavy fall or failure; a barber crops hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming a cropper means a collapse or flop, and a person who cuts hair short is one who crops.

clue.text: Goddess heard from you and some of 14

indicators.note: heard means what follows is spoken, so the letters are written as they sound

parts.note: the word you followed by the opening letters of 14-down, depravity, which begin turpi

explanation.surface: A deity whose voice comes through you and part of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'you' plus TURPI from TURPITUDE (14-down) sounds like the muse's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe was the Greek muse of music and lyric poetry, a minor goddess.

clue.text: Corrupt idler, man to do nothing

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy, dishonest fellow intent on idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie dormant is to stay inactive, like a seed waiting out the winter.

clue.text: Blast, for instance, into a thousand pieces

annotationWithheld.why: Blast, for instance, into a thousand pieces (4): Blast is an example of an oath, but no parse of 'into a thousand pieces' gives OATH (A THOU anagrammed has five letters); scan reads the same.
annotationWithheld.clue: Blast, for instance, into a thousand pieces

clue.text: Head pursues those lashing into a wee lad

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so this piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: whippers are people who lash with a whip
napper is old slang for the head

explanation.surface: A boss chases the floggers into a small boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursues' puts NAPPER after WHIPPERS; 'into a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is a cheeky young person, a mere boy.

clue.text: When hands meet and Englishmen go out

explanation.surface: A time when clock hands come together and English people step outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward's song says 'Mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun'.
explanation.definitionFit: At twelve o'clock both clock hands point straight up together, and in Coward's song the English venture out at midday.

clue.text: Escort a hundred assembled guests?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
company means a gathering of visitors

explanation.surface: Guiding a hundred guests who have gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to go along with them as a companion.

clue.text: Hire — daily terms reduced by thousands

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman, a char in British usage

indicators.note: reduced by means made smaller through losing these letters

parts.note: taken as written
M is a thousand, so Ms are thousands

explanation.surface: Engaging a cleaner on terms cut by thousands of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily, British slang for a charwoman, gives CHAR; TERMS loses M and S, the Ms of 'thousands'.
explanation.definitionFit: To charter a boat or plane is to rent it for exclusive use.

clue.text: Depravity is rude, put it differently

indicators.note: differently means in another arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Wickedness: it's crude however you phrase it.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is moral baseness or wickedness.

clue.text: Kneeler has leg-covering

parts.note: a sock covers the foot and lower leg

explanation.surface: Something to kneel on that comes with a stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a firm cushion for kneeling on in church.

clue.text: Hear from the eldest son, by letter

definitions.text: Hear from the eldest son, by letter

indicators.note: hear means the word is spoken, so heir is taken by its sound

parts.note: the eldest son is the heir
mail is letters and post

explanation.surface: A parent gets news from the firstborn abroad by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'by' link; as a whole the clue describes getting a letter flown from a son overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Post carried by aircraft is how families once got letters from relatives far away.

clue.text: Notices put up I shifted in part

indicators.note: shifted means the letter I is taken out and placed elsewhere
in a down entry, put up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Notices are posted and I am moved into another department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns NOTICES into SECITON; 'shifted' moves its I to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or division of a whole.

clue.text: Get furious about point having shown derision

indicators.note: about means around, so the phrase wraps the letter

parts.note: to see red is to get furious
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone angered over a remark after mocking others.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneered means mocked with scorn.

clue.text: Seeing that note is genuine

parts.note: since means because, seeing that
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Observing that a musical note rings true.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and heartfelt.

clue.text: Paints chap standing up surrounded by fish

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: eels are fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Artwork of an upright man ringed by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' reverses MAN to NAM; 'surrounded by' puts NAM inside EELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels are glossy paints that dry hard.

clue.text: Sweetheart put up presents

parts.note: dona or donah is old British slang for a sweetheart

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: set means put

explanation.surface: A lover hangs up gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SET to TES. DONA, from Spanish dona, was Victorian London slang for a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give, as one presents a gift.

clue.text: No medicament or treatment, that's the advice

indicators.note: treatment means handling or working over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor advising against drugs or any therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A recommendation is a suggestion about what to do, which is counsel.

clue.text: Roll of notes gets one a dry bed

parts.note: a wad is a bundle of banknotes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone with a fat roll of cash gets a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a desert watercourse that is dry outside the rainy season.

clue.text: A change for Neptune, left on the outside, last but two

indicators.note: change means altered, so the letters of the god's name are reordered
on the outside means only the first and last letters of left are used

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the god of the sea out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change for' rearranges NEPTUNE into NTEPENU; 'on the outside' takes L and T, the first and last letters of 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: The antepenult is the third syllable from the end of a word.

clue.text: Blue about rejected love, moving like a cat

indicators.note: about means around, so the colour surrounds the other piece

parts.note: sky blue, the sky being blue

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A sad lover spurned, prowling off like a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses NIL to LIN; 'about' puts SKY around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slinky means moving with a stealthy, smooth grace.

clue.text: But these defaulters of course could be Englishmen

definitions.text: But these defaulters of course could be Englishmen

parts.words: But these defaulters of course could be Englishmen
parts.note: people who fail to pay at the racecourse carry a name that sounds like a nationality, though they may be English

explanation.surface: A remark that some dodgers are, naturally, English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means at the racecourse, where bookmakers who skip paying out bets have a name sounding Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Welshers dodge debts, especially betting debts, so they default.
